name: blackswan
description: BlackSwan trains reinforcement-learning agents to trade a SINGLE crypto asset (BTCUSDT) on the spot market, long-only by default, under realistic 0.1% per-trade fees. Each run trains on historical klines and is tested OUT-OF-SAMPLE (walk-forward windows 2022/2023/2024, expanding train); the agent observes multi-timeframe OHLCV (e.g. stacked 1h+1d layers) plus optional technical indicators. The objective is traded_return = total post-fee return gated by trade frequency (trade often AND well — a near-hold run scores ~0). In the strong presets the agent has NO explicit sell action (no_sell_action): it only times entries and exits are forced by take-profit/stop-loss/trailing-stop — so 'many buys, few sells' is by design, not a bug. 'Good' = a setup that trades often and profitably AND beats buy-and-hold (positive return_vs_hold_pct) net of fees, stable across seeds and walk-forward windows.

pipelineChangelog.summary: Observation/reward ALIGNMENT fix in the multi-timeline (resolved-from-fidelity) data provider. MultiTimelineDataProvider.get_values omitted the warmup (start_index) from its observation offset, so the observation ended ~one lookback window BEHIND the bar get_price/the reward used (≈31 days for 1h+1d at lookback 32, scaling with the window). This is a STALE-observation desync, NOT a look-ahead leak — the agent saw OLD data, never the future, so returns were never inflated; but training credit-assignment was corrupted. Every MULTI-timeline run is affected and NOT comparable to v5: multi-layer (1h+1d / 1h+1d+1w / 1d+1w), a coarser single layer at a finer step (1d@1h), a finer base at a coarser step (1h@1d), or auto@1h (= 1h+1d). Those v<5 runs are marked status=invalid and excluded from all aggregation/xAI. SINGLE-timeline runs (1d@1d, 1h@1h, auto@1d) used the SingleDataProvider and are UNAFFECTED. Also lands daily-step multi-fidelity (a daily step can now observe finer/multi layers by stepping the 1h base day by day, divider 24) — additive, with end-to-end look-ahead regression guards; no impact on prior runs.

Correctness bug-fix sweep — scores are NOT comparable to v3 for affected setups. (1) Prioritized replay (DQN/Rainbow PER) was effectively UNIFORM: add() seeded each new transition into the wrong slot from an all-zero max, and a full buffer could NaN-crash sampling; new transitions now get the correct max-priority seed and sampling is stable, so PER models train differently. (2) Multi-timeline get_values with lookback<=1 now CONCATENATES layer features instead of element-wise SUMMING them, correcting observations for multi-layer lookback<=1 data configs. (3) Removed the dead 'combo2' reward model (it silently fell through to profit_percentage). Other fixes with no impact on the main training path: reward-multiplier scalar defaults (were (0,) tuples), dataclass default_factory landmines (net_arch / layers / Config lists), process_df 'expanded' timestamp_close coercion (feature-identical in production), GlobalContextAttention non-square contraction, env_factory error message, derive_cache _to_ms / empty-frame guards, R2Loss / SquaredMeanLoss numerics, the dip-env streak metric, and the GlobalContextAttention 2-D path (now usable inside the custom MLP). Removed dead code entirely: the whole server path (ServerCryptoEnv / ServerDataProvider / run_server_model / src.server websocket+cache / src.config) and the duplicate 'duel-dqn-custom-lstm8' factory branch.

Walk-forward evaluation: a walk_forward_window lever tests on 2022/2023/2024 with an expanding train window (default 2024 = train 2020-2023 / test 2024 reproduces the v2 single split EXACTLY, so v2 runs stay comparable to v3 window-2024 runs). Adds sharpe_alpha (risk-adjusted excess over buy-and-hold on the same window) to metrics and stamps the window into the dataset. Different windows are separate out-of-sample samples — group them, never compare a 2022 run to a 2024 run as one number.

Data + scoring overhaul: fidelity-scaled rolling windows (QW1) + taker-buy ratio (QW2), 1m-canonical derive-cache + runtime-computed indicators, trade-aware traded_return with a QUADRATIC trade gate, n_trades fixed to completed-trade count, benchmark vs-hold aligned via get_price, combo_noaction default 0 (no synthetic-short bias). Scores are NOT comparable to v1.
Original pipeline — the historical results_hour.ods ledger import (Sharpe-era, pre-overhaul). Kept for reference; not comparable to v2.

runInvalidations.reason: Trained on observations ~one warmup window behind the priced/rewarded bar (multi-timeline observation/reward desync, fixed in pipeline v5). Not comparable to v5 — re-run for a valid result.

model_name.description: The algorithm / policy. Naming conventions: a bare name is the vanilla SB3 build, '-custom' uses tuned network internals, '-lstm' adds a recurrent features-extractor, '-sbx' is the JAX/SBX build. 'attn-ppo' / 'tcn-ppo' are PPO over a true SEQUENCE features-extractor (self-attention / dilated-causal TCN) that reshapes the flat obs back to its bar grid and encodes over the lookback window — the principled modern-sequence architectures (vs reppo's LSTM); A/B them against reppo. 'reppo'/'reppo-custom' = RecurrentPPO; 'trpo'/'trpo-custom' = TRPO; 'a2c'/'a2c-custom' = A2C. DQN line: 'dqn'/'dqn-custom'/'dqn-lstm'/'dqn-sbx'; dueling 'duel-dqn*'; 'munchausen-*' add the Munchausen log-policy bonus; 'rainbow-dqn'/'rainbow-dqn-custom' add prioritized experience replay (importance-weighted sampling by TD-error). Distributional: 'iqn'/'iqn-custom' (implicit quantile) and 'qrdqn'/'qrdqn-custom' (quantile-regression). 'ars'/'ars-mlp' are Augmented Random Search (gradient-free) baselines. 'supervised-logreg' / 'supervised-gbm' are the NON-RL baseline: a classifier predicts next-bar direction from the same features and a fixed rule trades on it (the decisive 'is RL even the right tool?' control). 'momentum' is a deterministic time-series-momentum baseline (long when the trailing `momentum_lookback`-bar return is positive, flat otherwise — Moskowitz-style), a non-RL control to beat. 'hodl' is the buy-and-hold control.

reward_model.description: Which reward function shapes behaviour. combo_unified is the ONE shaped reward — a per-step WEIGHTED SUM of components, each a continuous lever: combo_sell/combo_buy/combo_positionprofitpercentage reward realized P&L on close / direction on open / held-position P&L; combo_direct adds the raw per-step PORTFOLIO return (direct RL — with every other weight 0 it IS the old profit_percentage_direct); combo_noaction weights price moves while flat; combo_wrongaction penalises wasted actions (a buy while long / sell while flat); combo_fee_penalty and combo_noop_penalty are explicit turnover / no-op penalties. It subsumes the retired combo_all/_fee/_noop/2 + profit_percentage_direct names as POINTS in that weight-space. The earlier profit_all2 / profit_percentage3 / profit_percentage_direct names were removed (profit_percentage3 had a reward-side look-ahead, like the dropped combo; the others don't fit the weight-space) — combo_unified is the single comparable reward.

combo_noaction.description: Reward multiplier applied to price moves while the agent is FLAT (no position). Default 0 = direction-neutral (a flat agent is neither rewarded nor punished for which way price moves). -1 bakes a synthetic-short incentive (rewards price falling while flat) — kept as a deliberate variant to probe, NOT the default, since the agent is long-only.

combo_wrongaction.description: Penalty (signed weight, ≤ 0) added when the agent emits a WRONG action — opening while already in position, or closing while flat. 0 = off (the default, ≈ the old combo_all). The old combo_all2 was this term turned on.

combo_noop_penalty.description: The penalty subtracted each time the agent emits a NO-OP trade — a buy while ALREADY holding the asset, or a sell while holding cash (the action can't change the position). 0 = off (the default). The old combo_all_noop was this turned on (0.001). It only bites RELATIVE to the trade reward (combo_sell): at the baked combo_sell=1000 a tiny penalty is washed out, so the range allows up to 0.5 and Exp 15 sweeps it AGAINST combo_sell. Sweep it to find how hard to discourage dead actions without suppressing real trades.

combo_fee_penalty.description: Weight on the per-trade turnover penalty (penalty = transaction_fee × this) that discourages over-trading/churn. 0 = off (the default). The old combo_all_fee was this turned on (1.0).

combo_sell.description: combo_unified weight on the REALIZED P&L when a position is closed (sell/cover or TP/SL) — the headline 'did this trade make money' term. Baked default 1000 (the old combo_all value).

combo_buy.description: combo_unified weight on the next-step price move in the agent's favour when a position is OPENED (long rewarded for price up, short for down). Baked default 0.1.

combo_positionprofitpercentage.description: combo_unified weight on the per-step change in held-position P&L while IN a position. Baked default 10.

combo_direct.description: combo_unified weight on the DIRECT per-step portfolio return (net_worth[t]/net_worth[t-1] − 1), added every step. 0 = off (the default). Set to 1 with every other weight 0 to reproduce the old profit_percentage_direct (direct RL); mix with the shaping terms to blend.

learning_rate.description: Optimizer step size. Too high diverges, too low learns slowly. ~0.0001 is the tuned default.

gamma.description: Discount factor for future reward (0–1). Higher = more far-sighted.

batch_size.description: Samples per gradient update. Larger is steadier but slower.

buffer_size.description: Replay-buffer capacity — how many past steps the agent can learn from.

learning_starts.description: Steps of random exploration before learning begins (fills the buffer). 20000 was best in past runs.

net_arch.description: Hidden-layer sizes of the policy network. Small nets (e.g. 512,64) won in past runs; the big 8192,512 overfit and lost.

optimizer_class.description: Gradient optimizer. RMSprop was the tuned choice.

activation_fn.description: Neuron activation function. CELU was the tuned choice.

episodes.description: How many passes over the training data. Too few underfits; the exploration schedule now anneals across episodes.

exploration_fraction.description: Fraction of training over which the exploration rate (epsilon) anneals from 1.0 to exploration_final_eps. Higher = explore longer before exploiting. DQN-family algorithms.

exploration_final_eps.description: Final exploration rate (epsilon) the schedule anneals to — the residual randomness kept late in training. DQN-family algorithms.

lookback_window.description: How many past bars per fidelity layer the agent observes each step (intraday paths only; the single daily path is fixed at 1). Wider = more context but a bigger network input.

asset.description: Which coin to train on. Only BTCUSDT has 1d/1h data today; altcoins need backfill (the data mine). DATASET setting — managed as named datasets, not a model knob.

timeframe.description: STEP frequency — how OFTEN the agent acts (1d = once per day, 1h = once per hour). This is separate from which timeframes it OBSERVES (the fidelity_set dataset lever). Minute data behaved like noise for the RL models.

fidelity_set.description: Observation LAYERS — which timeframes the agent sees AT ONCE at each step (separate from the STEP frequency, which is the timeframe lever). Higher layers are resampled from the base, so wider = more context but a bigger input. auto = follow timeframe (1h->1h+1d, 1d->1d). The loaded BASE is the finest layer in the set, and every coarser layer is resampled from it. At an HOURLY step (timeframe=1h): 1h (single), 1d (single coarser layer fed every hour, i.e. 1h+1d with the 1h dropped), 1h+1d, 1h+1d+1w, or 1d+1w. At a DAILY step (timeframe=1d): 1d (single), 1d+1w, OR finer/multi sets (1h, 1h+1d, 1h+1d+1w) — the 1h base is stepped day by day (divider 24), the symmetric counterpart of an hourly step observing a resampled 1d. DATASET setting — define named datasets (e.g. '1h' vs '1h+1d') in the Datasets tab. The only sub-hourly layers (none exist) would fail fast; everything selectable resolves.

walk_forward_window.description: Walk-forward evaluation window — which year to TEST on, training on every year before it (2024 = train 2020-2023 / test 2024, the historical split; 2023 = train 2020-2022 / test 2023; 2022 = train 2020-2021 / test 2022). Run all three to see whether a config is robust across different market regimes OUT-OF-SAMPLE rather than tuned to one lucky year. DATASET setting — each window is a separate dataset; read them as a distribution, never as a single number.

use_indicators.description: Add a curated set of indicators (RSI/Williams/Stochastic/Choppiness + tanh-squashed meanReversion/turbulence/OBV + a realized-vol regime and a trend-slope feature) as features, computed at RUNTIME from OHLCV — so it works on BOTH 1d and the 1m-derived 1h path. Past RL runs found indicators didn't help on 1d; re-test under v3 scoring with the added regime/trend context.

forward_horizon.description: SUPERVISED baseline only: the classifier's label is the SIGN of the return over the next N steps (1 = next bar). Longer horizons predict a slower trend rather than next-bar noise. Ignored by RL/hodl models.

prob_threshold.description: SUPERVISED baseline only: go long only when the classifier's P(up) exceeds this (0.5 = act on any edge; higher = trade only high-confidence signals, fewer trades). Ignored by RL/hodl models.

momentum_lookback.description: MOMENTUM baseline only: the trailing window (in bars) whose return SIGN sets the position — long when the price now exceeds the price this many bars ago, flat otherwise. Re-evaluated every bar. E.g. at 1d cadence 30 ≈ monthly, 252 ≈ Moskowitz's ~12-month time-series-momentum rule. Ignored by RL/supervised/hodl models.

obs_squash.description: Observation normalization experiment. Several base features exceed the declared [-1,1] observation bound and SB3 does NOT clip, so the network sees raw out-of-range values. none = leave as-is (historical); clip = clip features to [-1,1]; tanh = tanh-squash them. Does respecting the declared bound help or hurt?

transaction_fee.description: Per-trade fee fraction applied to each trade (models real cost; discourages churn). ENVIRONMENT setting — defines the market, not the model.

stop_loss.description: Auto-close a losing position at this drawdown fraction (0 = off). ENVIRONMENT setting — an exit mechanic, not the model.

take_profit.description: Auto-close a winning position at this gain fraction (0 = off). ENVIRONMENT setting — an exit mechanic, not the model.

trailing_take_profit.description: Trailing take-profit fraction that follows the price up (0 = off). ENVIRONMENT setting — an exit mechanic, not the model.

no_sell_action.description: Remove the explicit sell action — exits happen only via TP/SL. Performed well in past runs.

position_sizing.description: How much of the balance to deploy per entry. fixed = all-in (historical default). vol_target = scale the deployed fraction to target a constant volatility (size = vol_target / recent realized vol, clamped to [0.1, 1]) — risks less in turbulent regimes, the structural fix for 'churns many trades for ~+1%'.

vol_target.description: Target per-bar volatility for vol_target position sizing (higher = larger positions). Only used when position_sizing = vol_target.

allow_shorting.description: What the ENVIRONMENT allows: off = long-only (buy/close, 3-way action space), on = long+short (adds short(3)/cover(4), 5-way). It's a property of the env/action-space, not the model — managed as named environments (clone any env to a long+short variant). Test long-only vs long+short by running a model across both environments; short exits respect TP/SL (mirrored).

device.description: Compute device: cpu, mps (Apple GPU), or cuda (NVIDIA GPU).

seed.description: Random seed. The same seed reproduces a run exactly; different seeds measure variance.

papers.title: There are no Champions in Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
papers.authors: Brigato, Morand, Strommen, Panagiotou, Schmidt, Mougiakakou
papers.claim: Across 14 datasets and ~5000 trained nets, pairwise differences among DLinear/PatchTST/iTransformer/TimeMixer/TimeXer are mostly statistically INSIGNIFICANT (Friedman p~0.95); the 'champion' flips with setup + metric — no universal best forecaster.
papers.approach: Large-scale, statistically-rigorous re-benchmark of long-term TSF models.

assumptions.notes: long-horizon forecasting MSE/accuracy, not trading P&L or crypto

papers.verdictNote: Supports the WEAK form ('simpler TIES complex') and undercuts any blanket 'X wins'. For BlackSwan: demand a margin that survives multiple windows/seeds before crediting attn/tcn over the MLP.

papers.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?
papers.claim: A 1-layer linear model (DLinear/LTSF-Linear) outperforms FEDformer/Autoformer/Informer in all tested cases (often 20-50%); a naive repeat-last beats all Transformers ~45% on the financial Exchange-rate set — high-capacity Transformers overfit noisy series.
papers.approach: Strips Transformers to a linear baseline (trend+seasonal decomposition) across LTSF benchmarks.

assumptions.notes: forecasting MSE; contested by PatchTST/iTransformer

papers.verdictNote: Core SUPPORT for 'simpler wins on noisy financial data' — the prior reason to treat MLP/GBM as BlackSwan champions-to-beat. Contested (see the HF rebuttal blog).

papers.title: Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on typical tabular data?
papers.claim: Tree ensembles (XGBoost/RF/GBT) remain SOTA over deep nets on medium tabular data (~10K samples) even after ~20k compute-hours of tuning — NNs overfit irregular targets + uninformative features and are rotation-invariant.
papers.approach: Standardized benchmark of trees vs deep nets across 45 tabular datasets.

assumptions.notes: i.i.d. tabular, not time series — analogical transfer; gap narrows with more data

papers.verdictNote: Supports 'engineered-features -> tabular -> trees/MLP win' in BlackSwan's small-sample regime; grounds supervised-gbm as a hard baseline.

papers.title: Do We Really Need Deep Learning Models for Time Series Forecasting?
papers.claim: A window-based feature transformation lifts a simple GBRT to beat 7 of 8 SOTA deep baselines (incl. Exchange-rate); the lift comes from the INPUT transformation, not the learner. (Internal counter: TFT, an attention model, consistently beats GBRT.)
papers.approach: Reframes forecasting as tabular regression via windowed features, then GBRT.

assumptions.notes: forecasting metrics; one deep model (TFT) still beats GBRT

papers.verdictNote: The closest analog to BlackSwan's multi-timeframe stacking + supervised-gbm: engineered features carry the signal. Note the TFT counterexample.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Financial Time Series: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Risk-Adjusted Performance
papers.claim: Cross-asset daily-futures benchmark (rolling OOS + breakeven-cost analysis): hybrid LSTM/PatchTST models top by Sharpe (~2.3-2.4) with the largest cost buffer, while a temporally-aware linear (DLinear ~0.64) UNDERperformed a trivial AR(1).
papers.approach: Large-scale, cost-aware, risk-adjusted backtest of DL architectures across asset classes 2010-2025.

assumptions.notes: futures not single-asset crypto; doesn't test stacked-MLP/GBT

papers.verdictNote: REFUTES the strong 'simpler wins' form in a finance + COSTS setting — the key counter-evidence. For BlackSwan: sequence models CAN win on risk-adjusted P&L; the metric (P&L vs accuracy) is the pivot.

papers.title: Unlocking the Power of Patch: Patch-Based MLP for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
papers.claim: An attention-free patch-based MLP beats PatchTST and iTransformer on long-term forecasting — the recent gains come from PATCHING + channel handling, not attention.
papers.approach: Patch embedding + channel mixing/independence in a pure MLP.

assumptions.notes: forecasting MSE

papers.verdictNote: Supports 'the input handling / inductive bias matters more than attention' — a well-fed MLP can match transformers.

papers.title: Yes, Transformers are Effective for Time Series Forecasting (+ Autoformer)
papers.claim: Rebuttal to DLinear: a size-matched, properly-designed Transformer (plus RevIN for distribution shift) matches/beats the linear model — 'Transformers aren't ineffective, they were improperly used.'
papers.approach: Fair re-run of DLinear vs a comparable Transformer + Autoformer with normalization.

assumptions.notes: blog (not peer-reviewed); forecasting MSE

papers.verdictNote: Balancing/REFUTING the simpler-wins claim — argues linear-beats-transformer was a fairness artifact. Keep as the counterpoint to DLinear.

papers.title: The M5 competition: Results, findings, and conclusions
papers.claim: In the M5 competition (42,840 series), all top methods were pure ML; LightGBM was the most-used and the winner; DeepAR placed ~3rd and N-BEATS only at high aggregation.
papers.approach: The largest open forecasting competition (Walmart retail demand).

assumptions.notes: retail demand not finance; leans on POOLING across thousands of correlated series — not available single-asset

papers.verdictNote: Supports 'GBM wins' — but the edge comes from cross-series pooling, an advantage BlackSwan (single asset) does NOT have. Read with that caveat.

papers.title: Re(Visiting) Time Series Foundation Models in Finance
papers.claim: Across global markets, off-the-shelf time-series foundation models do NOT consistently beat a simple gradient-boosted tree; only heavy financial-domain pretraining helps.
papers.approach: Empirical eval of pretrained TSFMs vs simple baselines on financial forecasting.

assumptions.notes: cross-sectional equities, not single-asset crypto trading P&L

papers.verdictNote: Supports 'a simple GBT is a hard baseline in finance' even vs large pretrained models. Grounds the supervised-gbm baseline.

papers.title: An Application of Deep Reinforcement Learning to Algorithmic Trading
papers.claim: Introduces TDQN (Trading Deep Q-Network), a DQN adapted to single-asset algorithmic trading that trains one agent per instrument to maximize the annualised Sharpe ratio, using artificial-trajectory data augmentation. On a 30-instrument testbench it claims to outperform passive and active benchmarks on average, while candidly reporting mixed, asset-dependent results and overfitting on some stocks.
papers.approach: A five-layer feedforward Deep Q-Network learns a discrete long/short/neutral position policy per asset; training is bootstrapped from artificial trajectories synthesized from limited historical OHLCV, and the 0.1% trading cost is folded directly into the decision process. One model is trained per stock (single-asset, single-split OOS) with shared hyperparameters across the testbench.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Train once on 2012-2017, evaluate frozen policy on 2018-2019; no retraining/walk-forward, no online learning on the test set (DNN params fixed during test execution).
assumptions.notes: Single fixed train/test split per asset, NOT walk-forward; equities/indices only (no crypto); training leans on artificial-trajectory augmentation; a validation subset of the training set is used for hyperparameter tuning, so the test set is a single OOS holdout; authors explicitly acknowledge overfitting on some stocks (e.g. Tesla) and cite Bailey/Lopez de Prado backtest-overfitting risk.

papers.verdictNote: Ideal protocol match (single-asset, one agent per instrument, OOS test, 0.1% per-trade fees explicitly modelled and deducted), so it transfers cleanly to BTC. BUT the headline edge is thin: testbench AVERAGE Sharpe is TDQN 0.404 vs B&H 0.369, a marginal margin over a passive baseline in a mostly bullish 2018-2019 window, with highly dispersed per-asset results. The authors flag overfitting and reliance on artificial-trajectory augmentation. A 0.04-Sharpe single-split beat is fragile and unlikely to robustly survive walk-forward; on BTC the long-bias of B&H is even stronger, so 'beats B&H' could easily flip. Replicate as a baseline DRL method; treat 'beats B&H' as borderline/fluff-risk until reproduced walk-forward at 0.1% fees on BTC.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Trading
papers.authors: Zihao Zhang, Stefan Zohren, Stephen Roberts
papers.claim: Deep RL trading agents (DQN, Policy Gradient, A2C) over discrete and continuous action spaces, with volatility scaling, outperform classical time-series momentum baselines on 50 liquid futures and continue to deliver positive profits even under heavy transaction costs (up to ~25bp per trade).
papers.approach: Three deep RL algorithms — DQN (discrete {-1,0,1}), Policy Gradients (discrete), and A2C (continuous [-1,1]) — map normalised prices, multi-horizon returns (1/2/3-month, 1-year), MACD and RSI into a target position. Reward is volatility-scaled to size positions inversely to market volatility, then aggregated across a 50-contract diversified portfolio with vol-targeting.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Expanding-window retrain every 5 years with parameters frozen for the next 5-year block; OOS spans 2011-2019. Coarse two/three-fold walk-forward, NOT tight rolling re-train.
assumptions.notes: Headline Sharpe (1.288/1.050) is a 50-contract DIVERSIFIED, vol-targeted FUTURES portfolio — much of the Sharpe comes from cross-sectional diversification and vol-targeting, not the RL signal alone. Positions are long-AND-short and vol-scaled (continuous sizing). Costs modelled as bp-per-trade up to 25bp with explicit sensitivity curves. Profitability stated at portfolio level, not single-asset breakeven. Coarse 5-year retrain blocks risk regime-staleness.

papers.verdictNote: Highly-cited benchmark (Oxford-Man, JFDS 2020); the algorithm/feature menu (DQN/PG/A2C + momentum + MACD/RSI + vol-scaling) maps directly onto the registry. BUT headline Sharpe does NOT transfer to single-asset BTC spot: (1) it is a 50-contract diversified portfolio — diversification and vol-targeting carry most of the 1.0-1.3 Sharpe, gone for one asset; (2) long-AND-short continuous sizing vs long-biased; (3) futures cost structure (~25bp) is not the same as 0.1%=10bp round-trip on spot. Their 25bp tolerance is nominally above 10bp, encouraging IF it survives single-asset. The 5-year frozen-retrain walk-forward is coarse. Replicate the algorithm menu + vol-scaling, but independently re-verify 'survives heavy costs' at single-asset BTC under 0.1%/trade with a finer rolling retrain.

papers.title: Learning to Trade via Direct Reinforcement
papers.claim: Direct/recurrent reinforcement learning (RRL) — the policy outputs a trading position directly with no value function or price forecast, trained by gradient ascent on a risk-adjusted utility — discovers profitable trading systems while accounting for transaction costs. RRL outperforms Q-learning, and optimizing the differential Sharpe ratio yields more consistent results than maximizing profit; both beat a forecast/MSE-based trader. Demonstrates predictability in the monthly S&P 500 (1970-1994).
papers.approach: A recurrent policy maps recent returns/indicators plus its own prior position directly to a new long/short/neutral position; parameters trained by online gradient ascent on a risk-adjusted utility (the differential Sharpe ratio, an incrementally-updatable per-step reward), with an explicit transaction-cost penalty in the reward so the agent learns not to over-trade.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Online/incremental adaptive updating; reported on a single rolling historical path rather than a formal repeated walk-forward protocol.
assumptions.notes: Single-asset (one index / one FX pair), single historical path; monthly S&P 500 (1970-1994) and half-hourly USD/GBP FX. Costs modelled at ~0.5% round-trip on instruments far cheaper/less volatile than crypto. No multiple-trials / deflated-Sharpe correction, no formal multi-fold walk-forward, effectively single in-sample-tuned evaluation. Deliberately low turnover. Predates modern backtest-overfitting controls.

papers.verdictNote: Genuinely seminal POSITIVE method — the long/short single-asset RRL framing maps almost 1:1 onto long-biased single-BTC spot with optional shorting, and the in-reward transaction-cost term plus differential Sharpe are directly portable (this is the seed for our differential_sharpe reward). BUT original evidence is weak by the registry's bar: single historical path, no walk-forward / deflated-Sharpe, low turnover, ~0.5% costs on monthly/half-hourly traditional instruments. Crypto at 0.1%/trade with higher vol and far more decision points means cost drag and overfit risk are materially worse. Whether DSR-RRL clears 0.1% fees out-of-sample walk-forward on BTC is precisely the open question to TEST. Treat 2001 results as method-validation, not transferable numbers.

papers.title: The Recurrent Reinforcement Learning Crypto Agent
papers.authors: Gabriel Borrageiro, Nick Firoozye, Paolo Barucca
papers.claim: An echo-state-network feature space feeds a direct, recurrent reinforcement learning agent that trades the BitMEX XBTUSD Bitcoin perpetual swap intraday, maximizing a quadratic risk-adjusted utility with a transaction-cost penalty and online transfer learning. The agent reportedly realizes a 350% total return net of transaction costs over ~5 years, 71% of which is funding profit, at an annualized information ratio of 1.46.
papers.approach: A direct/recurrent RL agent (Moody-Saffell lineage) takes features from an echo state network (reservoir RNN) and outputs trading positions, trained online via transfer learning to maximize a quadratic risk-adjusted utility including an explicit transaction-cost penalty. Single instrument (XBTUSD perpetual swap on BitMEX), capturing directional moves and funding-rate carry.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Online (sequential/continual update each step via transfer learning); no fixed periodic retrain cadence.
assumptions.notes: Single historical path / one backtest over ~5 years; no deflated-Sharpe / multiple-trials correction, so headline IR is optimistic given many design choices. Online learning is expanding-window, not clean blocked walk-forward; no explicit OOS protocol/benchmark in abstract. Instrument is a leveraged PERPETUAL SWAP, not spot: 71% of the 350% is funding-rate harvest (structural carry absent on spot), so only ~29% is directional alpha. Exact bps cost not disclosed in abstract.

papers.verdictNote: Closest published match to the registry's setup (single-BTC, cost-aware, risk-adjusted reward, direct/recurrent RL) and a genuine positive method — but headline 350% / IR 1.46 will NOT transfer to a spot, long-biased, 0.1%-fee walk-forward mandate. ~71% of the return is perpetual funding carry that is structurally ABSENT on spot; residual directional alpha is only ~29% (~15%/yr gross). It trades a leveraged derivative, so leverage and funding distort the comparison. One historical path, no deflated-Sharpe / no clear blocked walk-forward or benchmark. The replicable kernel is the architecture (ESN/recurrent features + direct RL + utility with a cost penalty to suppress over-trading); treat the dollar/IR claims as derivative-and-funding-inflated, not spot directional edge.

papers.title: Enhancing Time Series Momentum Strategies Using Deep Neural Networks (Deep Momentum Networks)
papers.authors: Bryan Lim, Stefan Zohren, Stephen Roberts
papers.claim: Deep Momentum Networks inject deep-learning trading rules into the time-series-momentum vol-scaling framework, jointly learning trend estimation and position sizing by training the network directly on the Sharpe ratio of the signal. On 88 continuous futures, the Sharpe-optimized LSTM improved traditional momentum by more than 2x in the absence of transaction costs, and continued to outperform up to 2-3 bps of costs; a turnover-regularisation term lets the network internalise costs at run-time.
papers.approach: A supervised hybrid: an LSTM (and other DNNs) replaces hand-crafted trend/sizing rules in the classic time-series-momentum pipeline, outputting a position directly. Trained to maximise realised Sharpe (custom loss) rather than predict returns, with optional turnover regularisation for cost-awareness.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Expanding-window walk-forward: retrained periodically (~every 5 years) and evaluated on the subsequent OOS block over a multi-decade futures history.
assumptions.notes: Headline '>2x' is GROSS of costs. Results are a cross-sectional PORTFOLIO of 88 liquid futures, NOT single-asset and NOT crypto/spot. Outperformance is vol-scaled and diversified; the cost test uses a turnover-proportional model where edge survives only to ~2-3 bps. Walk-forward OOS is done properly, but no deflated-Sharpe / multiple-testing correction on the architecture/hyperparameter search.

papers.verdictNote: Seminal, but likely FLUFF as-is for this registry. (1) Cost cliff: the paper's own tests show edge dies past ~2-3 bps; the registry's 0.1% = 10 bps is ~4x that level, so the advantage almost certainly does NOT survive without aggressive turnover regularisation, and even then net edge is unproven. (2) Diversification dependence: the '>2x' gain is for an 88-contract portfolio where idiosyncratic noise averages out; on single BTC there is no cross-sectional averaging, so realised Sharpe will be far lower/noisier. (3) Slow mean-trending futures vs high-vol 24/7 crypto spot. (4) Symmetric long/short vol-scaled vs long-biased spot. Replicate ONLY as a learned-direction-plus-vol-scaling baseline with the turnover penalty cranked up and cost sensitivity re-validated at the full 10 bps before any 'genuinely good' claim.

papers.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for the Financial Portfolio Management Problem
papers.authors: Zhengyao Jiang, Dixing Xu, Jinjun Liang
papers.claim: A model-free deep RL framework (EIIE topology + Portfolio-Vector Memory + Online Stochastic Batch Learning, realized as CNN/RNN/LSTM, trained by deterministic policy gradient on a log-return reward) for cryptocurrency portfolio management achieves at least 4-fold returns in 50 days even at a high 0.25% commission rate, with all three network instances occupying the top three positions against benchmark portfolio-selection algorithms.
papers.approach: An Ensemble of Identical Independent Evaluators (EIIE) — weight-shared CNN/RNN/LSTM scoring each asset independently — outputs portfolio weights via softmax; trained end-to-end by deterministic policy gradient to maximize average log accumulated return, with a Portfolio-Vector Memory feeding prior weights to penalize turnover and Online Stochastic Batch Learning for continual updates.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Online Stochastic Batch Learning (continual mini-batch updates); reported results are a single chronological train/backtest split, not rolling walk-forward.
assumptions.notes: Models 0.25% commission (above the 0.1% target) but NO slippage/market-impact or liquidity/fill constraints. Pre-set top-12 coins by volume introduces survivorship/look-ahead bias. Single short ~50-day OOS window over the 2017 bull run; no Sharpe, no deflated/multiple-testing correction. Self-reported by the model's authors; high turnover at 30-min bars.

papers.verdictNote: Seminal and heavily cited (foundational to the EIIE/PVM lineage behind FinRL), but the headline 4x/50-day result is the textbook FLUFF-to-disprove case. It is a 12-COIN PORTFOLIO, not single-asset BTC, so not directly comparable to a long-biased BTC spot target. The backtest is a single ~2-month OOS window inside the 2017 bull regime — almost certainly regime-overfit; pre-selected top-volume coins inject survivorship/look-ahead bias. 0.25% commission is modelled (above target) but there is no slippage/market-impact, and 30-min rebalancing implies heavy turnover real fills would erode. No Sharpe, no PBO/deflated-Sharpe, no rolling walk-forward. Use as a methodology/architecture reference (EIIE, PVM, policy-gradient log-return reward), NOT as a credible return claim — a single-asset port loses the cross-asset weighting that is the whole mechanism.

papers.title: Time Series Momentum
papers.authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
papers.claim: A simple time-series momentum rule — go long (short) over the next month if the past 12-month excess return was positive (negative), sizing each position to a constant ex-ante volatility target — generates significant, persistent abnormal returns. Significant for each of 58 liquid futures/forwards across equity indices, currencies, commodities and bonds; a diversified TSM portfolio earns substantial alpha with little factor exposure and performs best in extreme markets.
papers.approach: A single-instrument trend rule: the sign of the trailing 12-month excess return sets a long/short position for the next month, each position scaled by inverse ex-ante (rolling) volatility to target constant risk (the diversified portfolio scaled to ~40% vol, realizing ~12%). Positions are equal-risk-weighted and aggregated across 58 futures/forwards.

assumptions.retrainCadence: None — fixed parametric rule (12-month lookback, 1-month hold), no training/refit; full-sample in-sample parameter choice.
assumptions.notes: Headline results are GROSS of transaction costs (robust to low futures costs, but reported Sharpe is essentially pre-cost); long-AND-short; uses leverage/vol-targeting to ~40% vol (12% realized); 58-instrument DIVERSIFIED portfolio — the ~1.2 Sharpe is cross-asset, NOT single-asset; sample 1985-2009 predates crypto; full-sample parameter selection (single lookback/hold, no walk-forward optimization but also no OOS holdout).

papers.verdictNote: Replicated via the deterministic `momentum` model (long when the trailing momentum_lookback-bar return is positive, flat otherwise; long/flat single-asset BTC spot, fixed sizing — vol-target sizing deferred as a multi-asset precursor, shorting a future extension), swept over 30/90/252-bar lookbacks. Seminal, but transplanting the ~1.2 Sharpe to single-asset spot BTC under 0.1% fees + walk-forward is unjustified for three compounding reasons. (1) Diversification: the strong Sharpe is a 58-instrument cross-asset portfolio; a single asset loses nearly all the variance reduction — expect single-asset TSM Sharpe far lower (often <0.5). (2) Costs: results are essentially GROSS; 0.1%/trade spot fees plus a vol-scaled frequently-resized rule bleed materially, and crypto's high vol forces more turnover. (3) The registry is long-biased spot, so the short leg (TSM's crisis-alpha) is constrained, cutting return. Net: TSM is the RIGHT honest, parameter-light non-ML CONTROL to beat — a deep model that cannot beat this adapted, net-of-fee, walk-forward control is fluff.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Bitcoin Trading Under Transaction Costs: Evidence From Walk-Forward Forecasting
papers.claim: Machine-learning forecasts (XGBoost, LSTM, iTransformer) of hourly BTC-USDT returns produce positive GROSS trading returns, but naive sign-based strategies COLLAPSE once 10 bps (0.1%) per-trade costs are imposed; a cost-aware turnover/execution filter that trades only when forecast magnitude exceeds the cost threshold restores net profitability for selected configurations, with the strongest long-only XGBoost variant reaching ~65.4% annualized return and Sharpe ~1.09 — only marginally above buy-and-hold (~56.3% / Sharpe 0.82).
papers.approach: Forecast-then-trade supervised ML (NOT reinforcement learning): XGBoost, LSTM, iTransformer forecast next-hour BTC-USDT returns; point predictions are converted to long/short (or long-only) positions via sign rules, optionally gated by a cost-aware filter suppressing trades unless the predicted move exceeds round-trip cost. Evaluated OOS in a 27-fold walk-forward over ~70k hourly bars (2018-2026), all returns net of 10 bps per-position-change.

assumptions.retrainCadence: Walk-forward: model refit each of 27 sequential folds (rolling/expanding train -> next OOS block).
assumptions.notes: Single-asset BTC-USDT, hourly. 10 bps treated as an 'all-in effective' per-trade cost per unit of turnover, not just exchange fees — matches the registry's 0.1% standard. No slippage/market-impact beyond the flat 10 bps. Genuine multi-fold walk-forward OOS. Holm correction on bootstrap dominance tests, BUT the 'restored' Sharpe>1 result is for SELECTED winning configurations across many model/feature/threshold specs -> config-selection bias; no Deflated Sharpe / PBO on the winning config.

papers.verdictNote: HIGH constructive-skeptic value: directly demonstrates the registry's central thesis — sign-based ML that looks great gross is FLUFF once a realistic 0.1% per-trade fee applies, because turnover dominates the edge. The restored result is fragile: cost-aware long-only XGBoost Sharpe ~1.09 / ~65.4% barely exceeds B&H (~0.82 / ~56.3%), so most apparent edge is just BTC's bull drift, and the win is a SELECTED configuration with no DSR/PBO deflation. The 27-fold walk-forward and net-of-cost reporting are sound; under the registry's 0.1% + walk-forward bar, naive strategies clearly FAIL and the filtered strategy only marginally survives, likely losing Sharpe>1 after deflation. Best as a calibration/skeptical anchor and a single-asset BTC walk-forward template — replicate the cost-aware filter and apply DSR/PBO to its winning spec.

papers.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
papers.authors: David H. Bailey, Marcos López de Prado
papers.claim: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) is a statistical correction returning the probability a reported Sharpe reflects genuine skill rather than the luck of multiple testing. It deflates the observed Sharpe for (a) the number of independent trials N — via the expected maximum Sharpe under the null (the 'False Strategy Theorem') — and (b) the non-normality of returns (skewness/kurtosis) and finite track-record length T, separating legitimate findings from statistical flukes.
papers.approach: Compute DSR = Φ((SR* − SR₀)·√(T−1) / √(1 − γ₃·SR* + ((γ₄−1)/4)·SR*²)), where SR₀ is the expected maximum Sharpe of N unskilled trials (depends on N and cross-trial variance of Sharpe estimates), and γ₃, γ₄ are return skewness/kurtosis. A high DSR (near 1) means the Sharpe survives correction for selection bias and fat tails; a low DSR flags an overfit/lucky result.

assumptions.retrainCadence: N/A — an evaluation/significance metric, not a trained strategy; applied post hoc to any candidate's OOS Sharpe and to the count of trials tried during selection.
assumptions.notes: Methodology/metrics paper (no return/Sharpe of its own; models no costs). Requires an HONEST count of independent trials N (estimated via clustering of correlated trials) — under-reporting N defeats the deflation. The False Strategy Theorem uses an extreme-value approximation under a normal null; skewness/kurtosis corrections are first-order finite-sample estimates.

papers.verdictNote: A SKEPTICAL/methodology entry — not a strategy to replicate. It does not 'survive fees' or 'beat buy-and-hold'; it is the GATE to apply to every RL/ML candidate's OOS Sharpe. The single most actionable multiple-testing correction for this registry given crypto's fat tails and the dozens of hyperparameter/feature/seed configs that will be tried. CRITICAL: the DSR is only as honest as the logged trial count N — if the registry under-reports the true number of independent configs explored (or treats correlated trials as one), the deflation is silently defeated. Note DSR deflates a Sharpe but does NOT incorporate the 0.1% fee drag, so apply it to the net-of-fees, walk-forward Sharpe. Widely cited, no replication controversy (it is math).

papers.title: Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism: The Effects of Backtest Overfitting on Out-of-Sample Performance
papers.authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos López de Prado, Qiji Jim Zhu
papers.claim: Trying even a modest number of alternative strategy configurations on the same data almost guarantees a high in-sample Sharpe with zero expected out-of-sample performance; the more configurations tried, the higher the probability the backtest is overfit. They derive a 'Minimum Backtest Length' (MinBTL): the backtest must be long enough relative to the number of independent trials N, otherwise the best in-sample Sharpe is pure overfitting. Because analysts rarely report how many configurations were tried, the degree of overfitting is usually unknowable.
papers.approach: A statistical/theoretical proof: under repeated trials, the expected maximum in-sample Sharpe of N independent random strategies grows with N (roughly proportional to sqrt(2 ln N)), so selecting the best backtest yields a strategy whose true OOS Sharpe is ~0. They invert this into MinBTL = minimum years of (IID) returns needed before the highest-in-sample Sharpe among N trials can be distinguished from luck.

assumptions.retrainCadence: N/A — a methodology/theory paper; the result concerns how many configurations/trials are run, not a training cadence.
assumptions.notes: Methodology paper, no own returns to net of costs. Core bound assumes (near-)IID Gaussian returns and a researcher optimizing/selecting on the evaluation window; real trials are usually correlated, so the EFFECTIVE number of independent trials N (and thus MinBTL) must be estimated. Under serial-dependence the OOS expectation is NEGATIVE, not merely zero. It quantifies the danger of selection across trials; not a per-strategy verdict.

papers.verdictNote: A SKEPTICAL/methodology cornerstone — does not 'survive 0.1% fees + walk-forward OOS' because it makes no return claim; it is the calibration tool for judging everything else. Direct application: if a candidate model does not report how many configs/hyperparameters/seeds/lookbacks were tried, its walk-forward Sharpe cannot be trusted, and the Deflated Sharpe is the companion correction. MinBTL tells us whether our walk-forward windows are even long enough given how many BlackSwan presets we sweep. Caveat: its clean bound assumes IID-ish returns and test-window optimization, so it OVER-states danger for genuinely held-out walk-forward and UNDER-states it when trials are highly correlated — estimate the effective N. Highly cited, not subject to replication failure (it is a proof).

papers.title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting
papers.authors: Liu, Hu, Zhang, Wu, Wang, Ma, Long
papers.claim: Inverting the Transformer — tokenising each VARIATE's whole series (not each timestep) so self-attention models cross-variate correlations and the FFN learns per-series representations — beats vanilla Transformers and specialised models on multivariate long-term forecasting, with better generalisation to unseen variates. No new components, only inverted dimensions.
papers.approach: Embed each variate's full lookback series as one token; self-attention ACROSS variate tokens (no temporal positional encoding — variates are unordered); a per-variate feed-forward network; LayerNorm over variates.

assumptions.retrainCadence: N/A — a forecasting-architecture paper, not a trading strategy.
assumptions.notes: Forecasting benchmark (MSE/MAE on ETT/Traffic/Weather/etc.), not trading. The open question is whether inverted cross-variate attention helps a single-asset RL policy on a noisy OHLCV+portfolio observation under 0.1% fees.

papers.verdictNote: The architecture we A/B as `itransformer-ppo` (src/model/custom/sequence_extractor.py, encoder='itransformer') against attn-ppo (attention over time) and tcn-ppo. Per no-champions-tsf-2025, expect a near-wash on a single noisy asset — the value is the rigorous A/B under walk-forward + fees, not a regime oracle.

models.name: Recurrent PPO (custom LSTM)
models.description: On-policy PPO with an LSTM that carries state across bars plus a regularised custom actor-critic head. The default/winner and the closest practical realisation of direct/recurrent RL on a risk-adjusted utility.

models.name: PPO
models.description: Proximal Policy Optimization (clipped surrogate, on-policy). Covers the stock SB3 MLP policy, the custom regularised actor-critic head (ppo-custom), and the JAX/SBX build.

models.name: TRPO
models.description: Trust-region (KL-constrained) policy gradient; covers the custom-head and stock-MLP variants.

models.name: Attention-PPO
models.description: PPO over a true sequence features-extractor: single-block self-attention with a learned positional embedding over the reshaped bar grid (vs reppo's LSTM).

models.name: DQN
models.description: Deep Q-network (replay buffer + target net). Covers the stock MLP policy, the custom head, the LSTM features-extractor variant, and the JAX/SBX build.

models.name: Dueling DQN
models.description: Off-policy Q-learning with separate value + advantage streams. Consolidates every dueling variant: custom head, the LSTM features-extractor flavours (hidden 2/3/4), and the stock dueling policy.

models.name: Munchausen DQN
models.description: DQN augmented with the Munchausen term (a scaled log-policy bonus added to the reward) — implicit KL-regularised policy iteration. Consolidates the plain, custom-head, and dueling+LSTM Munchausen variants.

models.name: Rainbow DQN
models.description: DQN with prioritized experience replay, NoisyNet exploration, dueling streams and distributional quantiles. Consolidates the custom head and the SB3-subclass build.

models.name: Implicit Quantile Network (IQN)
models.description: Distributional RL that samples implicit quantiles of the return distribution (quantile-Huber loss); covers the stock and custom-quantile-network variants. Implemented in code, not in the active sweep set.

models.name: Agent57
models.description: DQN with an Agent57-style intrinsic-reward exploration buffer (count-based + prediction-error + episodic-memory novelty). Fixed 2026-06-26: CustomAgent57ReplayBuffer now records the sampled buffer positions (last_sampled_indices) so compute_intrinsic_rewards can look the per-sample bonus up — SB3's ReplayBufferSamples carries no indices.

models.name: Ensemble (4x Dueling DQN)
models.description: A bagged ensemble of four custom dueling-DQN agents. Trains each member independently and predicts by AVERAGING their Q-values then argmax (the discrete-action ensemble vote). Fixed 2026-06-26: reimplemented as a plain duck-typed model (learn/predict/save/policy/device) instead of an unfinished OffPolicyAlgorithm subclass.

models.name: Supervised (logistic regression)
models.description: Non-RL control: a logistic-regression classifier predicts next-bar direction from the same features and a fixed rule trades on it through the unchanged environment.

models.name: Supervised (gradient-boosted trees)
models.description: Non-RL control: a gradient-boosted-tree classifier (the decisive 'is RL even the right tool?' baseline) forecasting next-bar direction.

models.name: Buy-and-Hold
models.description: Passive control - buys at the first bar and holds to the end; the benchmark every active model must beat out-of-sample net of fees.

models.name: iTransformer sequence encoder (PPO)
models.description: PPO over an inverted-attention (iTransformer, Liu et al. 2024) sequence encoder — each VARIATE (feature column) is a token embedding its full lookback series, with attention ACROSS variates (no positional embedding; variates are unordered). A third SequenceFeaturesExtractor variant to A/B against attn-ppo (attention over time) and tcn-ppo. Built 2026-06-26 (sequence_extractor.py `encoder='itransformer'`).

models.name: A2C
models.description: Advantage Actor-Critic — a synchronous on-policy actor-critic. Covers the stock SB3 MLP build and the tuned custom-net-arch head.

models.name: QR-DQN
models.description: Quantile-Regression DQN — distributional RL that learns a set of return quantiles (via quantile-Huber regression) instead of a single Q-value. Covers the SB3-contrib build and the custom quantile net.

models.name: ARS
models.description: Augmented Random Search — a gradient-free baseline that perturbs policy weights along random directions and keeps the best. A decisive control: if random search rivals the gradient learners, the learned gradient isn't earning its keep.

models.name: Time-Series Momentum
models.description: A non-RL time-series-momentum baseline (Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen 2012): take a long/short position on the sign of the trailing return over a lookback. The rule-based trend-following control — 'does a learned policy actually beat simple momentum net of fees?'.

models.name: Recurrent Reinforcement Learning (RRL)
models.description: Moody & Saffell (2001) DIRECT recurrent RL — no Q-values, no SB3. A recurrent linear policy F_t = tanh(w·x_t + u·F_{t-1} + b) outputs a CONTINUOUS position in [-1,1] (the previous position feeds back, so it holds through noise), trained by gradient ASCENT on the Sharpe ratio of the realised strategy return R_t = F_{t-1}·r_t − δ·|ΔF| (the objective the online DIFFERENTIAL Sharpe estimates), via truncated BPTT. Single-asset; the continuous position is discretised to the env's discrete long/flat/short actions at eval.

models.name: ESN-RRL (Echo State Network + RRL)
models.description: Borrageiro (2022) — RRL on top of a fixed ECHO STATE NETWORK reservoir. A random recurrent net, scaled to a sub-unit spectral radius (the echo-state property), is run over the inputs WITHOUT training; its high-dimensional leaky-integrator state is the feature the trained RRL position layer reads (only the readout learns). Inherits RRL's direct Sharpe-ascent training + discretised-action eval; only the feature map differs.

models.name: TDQN (Trading Deep Q-Network)
models.description: Théate & Ernst (2021) Trading DQN — a deep double-DQN for single-asset trading. Mechanically the custom-head DQN (CustomDQNPolicy); its faithful identity is the LAUNCH CONFIG: a deep feedforward Q-net (e.g. 256-128-64 + BatchNorm), a low discount (gamma≈0.4), long/short positioning, and indicator inputs — carried by the paper's replicate spec. Selectable as model_name 'tdqn'.
